comparator.name: Bachelor Psychologie
comparator.sourceNotes: The current 180-EC bachelor comprises 120 EC of compulsory psychology and research courses, a 25-EC restricted-choice block from minor offerings, 20 EC of free elective space and a 15-EC bachelor thesis. The restricted-choice block is reconstructed neutrally to represent all five master-preparatory minor areas: select the first course in official minor order for each area, skipping any course already selected for an earlier area. This yields PB1802, PB2522, PB2012, PB2112 and PB2212; the choice was made independently of UCR fit.

routeSelection.basis: The generic programme permits a 25-EC restricted-choice block from its minor offerings. To represent Psychology broadly rather than privilege one professional route, one course is selected for each of the five master-preparatory minor areas in official order, skipping duplicates already selected for an earlier area.

alternatives.label: Broad psychology, behaviour & research
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum spans social, cognitive, biological, clinical, health and developmental psychology with quantitative and qualitative research methods.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to the broad OU Psychology bachelor: a multi-perspective study of behaviour and mind integrating biological, cognitive, social, developmental, health and clinical psychology with research design, statistics and qualitative inquiry.
progression: Biological, behavioural, social and research foundations precede statistics, cognition, health, abnormal and developmental psychology, an advanced research seminar, psychodiagnostics and higher-level interdisciplinary study. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; twelve 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Clinical, health & lifespan psychology
alternatives.labelReason: This curriculum centres psychological problems, health, development, assessment and intervention while retaining biological, social and research foundations.
alternatives.concept: A clinical-and-health direction examining psychopathology, health, development across the lifespan, diagnosis, psychotherapy and resilience alongside epidemiology, physiology, pharmacology, disease mechanisms and psychological research.
progression: Behavioural, biological, social and research foundations precede statistics, cognition, health, psychopathology and development, followed by epidemiology, pharmacology, disease mechanisms, ethics and psychodiagnostics. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; twelve 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes clinical, biomedical, health and lifespan applications the organising priority. It replaces four upper-level philosophy and communication courses in the closest programme with epidemiology, pharmacology, disease mechanisms and ethics, differing by exactly four courses and 30 EC in each direction.

alternatives.label: Brain, cognition & behavioural science
alternatives.labelReason: This curriculum centres neural, biological and computational mechanisms of cognition and behaviour while preserving core psychology and research training.
alternatives.concept: A brain-and-cognition direction combining neurobiology, perception, higher-order cognition and psycholinguistics with physiology, anatomy, genetics, laboratory science, data analysis and machine learning to investigate behaviour mechanistically.
progression: Brain, behaviour, life-science and social foundations precede neurobiology, molecular biology, data, statistics, health and abnormal psychology, then laboratory science, anatomy, disease, higher cognition, machine learning, genetics and advanced psychology research. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes neural, biological and computational explanation the organising priority. It differs from the closest programme by nine courses and 67.5 EC in each direction, and from the clinical route by seven courses and 52.5 EC in each direction.

blocks: Both introduce psychology through biological, cognitive and behavioural perspectives; OU provides a broader 10-EC disciplinary survey.
Both cover theories and evidence about social influence, cognition and interpersonal behaviour.
Both address agency, personality and the self, but OU presents these within clinical and personality psychology while UCR adds philosophical analysis.
Both develop interpersonal communication awareness; OU teaches structured conversational practice, while UCR focuses persuasive communication.
UCR integrates historical context in individual courses but lacks a selected dedicated history-of-psychology module.
UCR covers social behaviour and organisations indirectly but lacks a selected dedicated introduction to work and organisational psychology.
UCR has adjacent social and resilience study but no selected dedicated work-proactivity course.
Both introduce research design, measurement, experiments and statistics.
Both provide qualitative research design, interviewing and interpretation.
Both develop experimental methods and statistical analysis for behavioural research.
Both develop empirical data analysis; OU focuses cross-sectional psychological research.
Both examine prediction and evaluation from data; OU focuses psychological measurement and decision theory.
Both require critical synthesis of psychological literature and research reporting; UCR extends this into an advanced seminar.
UCR teaches scientific reasoning across its research courses but lacks a separate selected introduction-to-science module.
UCR includes research design and statistics but lacks a selected dedicated longitudinal-research practicum.
The OU thesis is a required 15-EC collaborative empirical psychology project; UCR optional independent research is shown in parallel as a comparison-only opportunity.
Both apply psychological theory and evidence to health, stress and illness.
Both examine mental disorders and psychopathology.
Both examine psychological development across the lifespan.
Both address adolescent development and resilience; UCR focuses vulnerability to extremism.
Both examine psychological assessment and diagnosis; UCR also covers psychotherapies.
Both connect evidence and health interventions at population or digital-health scale, with different disciplinary emphasis.
UCR includes communication and psychological study but lacks a selected dedicated psychological-interviewing practicum.
UCR covers health and social behaviour but lacks a selected dedicated work-and-health psychology module.
UCR covers abnormal psychology, diagnosis and therapies across courses but lacks a second dedicated clinical diagnosis-and-therapy module.
UCR lifespan psychology includes ageing, but no separate selected older-adult psychology course is presented as equivalent.
Both provide biological and evolutionary foundations relevant to behaviour; OU applies them directly to evolutionary psychology.
Both examine neural mechanisms underlying behaviour; OU combines this with neuropsychology and psychopharmacology.
Both examine the biological and cognitive bases of higher mental functions.
OU retains 20 EC of free elective space; UCR flexibility is expressed through the complete selected 180-EC programmes rather than a separate unassigned block.

notes.text: Open Universiteit provides a prescribed psychology sequence with dedicated historical, work-and-organisational, psychometric, interviewing and longitudinal-research courses, a 25-EC restricted-choice block and a formal 15-EC empirical thesis. UCR can assemble substantial social, cognitive, biological, clinical, health and developmental psychology with research methods, but does not reproduce that complete professional and methodological sequence.

selection.assessment: The closest programme integrates broad psychology with quantitative and qualitative research. Clinical/health/lifespan and brain/cognition form two further evidenced, coherent and mechanically feasible directions. They differ pairwise by at least 30 EC, so production stops at the three-alternative maximum.
